$comment: Source of truth for ~/.kn9t/config.toml. `cargo run -p xtask -- generate` renders docs/CONFIG.md from this file; scripts/check-schema.sh fails on drift. The parser in crates/kn9t-server/src/config.rs is authoritative for behaviour (R-TUI-012) — this file must describe what it actually accepts, and a mismatch is a bug in this schema or in the parser, not in the generated doc.

groups.heading: Top level
groups.description: Keys that sit at the root of the file, outside any table. Project-local config files may set these too; `[policy]` is global-only.

fields.description: Model id used for new sessions. `provider:id` or a bare `id` when unambiguous. Absent → the first declared `[[model]]`.
Model used to auto-title a session after its first assistant turn. Absent → the session's own model. A cheap model here saves money; titling is best-effort and never fails a turn.

groups.heading: Models — `[[model]]`
groups.description: An array of tables: one entry per model the server may be asked to run. `provider` must match a declared `[provider.<name>]`.

fields.description: Name of the `[provider.<name>]` table that serves this model.
Model id as kn9t refers to it (sessions store this).
Wire model id actually sent to the provider. Absent → `id`.
Context window in tokens. Drives the compaction / truncation ladder.
Maximum output tokens requested per turn.
Reasoning effort.
USD per million input tokens, used for cost reports.
USD per million output tokens.
USD per million cached input tokens read.
USD per million cached input tokens written.
Prompt-cache strategy for this model.
Number of cache breakpoints to place.
Minimum prefix size before a breakpoint is worth placing.
Per-model overrides of the provider's wire quirks.

groups.heading: Provider quirks
groups.description: Wire-format deviations from the OpenAI default (DESIGN §8.2). `RawQuirks` is shared: a model-level `quirks` overrides the provider-level one field by field. Absent fields fall back to the provider defaults.

fields.description: Request key that carries the output cap (`max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, …).
Role name for the system prompt.
Whether usage arrives on the SSE stream.
Whether a `finish_reason` is emitted.
How reasoning content is carried on the wire.
Whether a tool result carries the tool name alongside its id.
Provider thinking-block dialect.
How prior thinking is replayed in later requests.
Whether the tools array is mandatory on every request.
Whether the endpoint supports streaming.
Whether trailing whitespace is trimmed from messages.
Header used to carry a session id to the provider.
OpenAI surface to use (R-OAI-060).

groups.heading: Providers — `[provider.<name>]`
groups.description: One table per provider, keyed by the name `[[model]]` entries refer to. `kind` selects the provider implementation.

fields.description: `openai` for an HTTP endpoint, or `plugin` for a provider plugin subprocess.
Required for `kind = "openai"`. Base URL of the endpoint.
Bearer token for `kind = "openai"`, if the endpoint needs one.
Required for `kind = "plugin"`: binary name or absolute path.
Environment variables injected into the plugin subprocess. Values support `env:VAR` interpolation.
Extra request headers (R-SRV-CFG-010, `openai` only).
Fetch `/models` and register discovered models. Set `false` to skip auto-discovery (R-SRV-CFG-030).
Skip TLS certificate verification. Intended for local test endpoints only.
Provider-wide wire quirks, overridable per model.

groups.heading: Server — `[server]`
groups.description: Optional runtime knobs. All fields are optional and take the defaults shown; `0` disables a deadline or, for `max_turns`, means unbounded. `[server]` is not hot-reloaded by `POST /config/reload`.

fields.description: Seconds of inactivity (no attached clients, no running turns) before the server exits. `0` disables auto-exit.
Seconds a tool call waits for a human approval before denial. `0` waits forever. A backstop, so a client that disappears mid-prompt cannot pin the turn thread.
`interaction_request` wait with a live cancellable turn. `0` disables the deadline.
`interaction_request` wait with NO cancellable turn. Nothing can interrupt such a wait, so this deadline is the only exit. `0` disables the deadline.
Milliseconds a cancelled tool batch waits for a `parallel_safe` tool to notice `Cancel` before the loop synthesises a result and ends the turn. Raise for slow tools, lower to make ESC snappier.

Optional spend guard: maximum turns one run may take before it stops with "turn limit reached". **Absent or `0` means unbounded** — the loop runs until it goes idle or the user aborts, which is the default. Set a positive value only to cap a model that never goes idle.

groups.heading: Policy — `[policy]`
groups.description: Global only (~/.kn9t/config.toml), never read from a project-local file. ADR-0008 moved risk decisions into the policy plugin; `mode` survives as a reporting value, and `[policy.approvals]` persists `scope=always` grants.

fields.description: Reporting value for the active policy posture.
Persistent approval grants.

groups.heading: Policy approvals — `[policy.approvals]`
groups.description: Written by the server when a user answers an approval with `scope=always`. Never hand-edit the `always` list; the `never` entries are managed separately.

fields.description: Fingerprints of approvals the user chose to always allow.

groups.heading: Plugins — `[[plugin]]`
groups.description: An array of tables overriding plugin discovery (ADR-0004, R-PLUG-100): `cmd` pins a path, `env` alone injects vars, `enabled = false` / `disabled = true` suppresses the discovered plugin of the same name. Global-only; a project-local file cannot honor a plugin entry.

fields.description: Matches the plugin's declared name (usually its binary file name); used for dedup.
Command plus args to spawn. Omit (or set `enabled = false`) for an env-only override or a disable entry.
Environment variables to inject. Values support `env:VAR` syntax.
`false` disables the discovered plugin of the same name.
Alias for `enabled = false`. If `true`, the plugin is disabled.
